transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, it’s probably not a huge thing, but my wife’s been noticing it more. She’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides and I’m looking right at her, trying to listen, and then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said. So… I guess that’s what made me think I should come in and ask about it, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing or getting distracted easily in other situations, like while reading, working, or driving?

Yeah, I’d say so… not all the time, but enough that I’ve noticed it. Like if I sit down to work out a catering order, or I’m on one of those parish planning calls, I start out paying attention just fine. Then after a bit my mind kind of drifts, and I’ll look back at the notes and realize I need to read the same part again like I didn’t really take it in the first time. It’s not terrible, I don’t think, but it does happen.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking or memory, like forgetting things more often, having trouble organizing your thoughts, or feeling mentally slowed down?

A little bit, yeah. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve been forgetting some ordinary things I meant to do… like returning a call from the doctor’s office, or picking up a prescription. And a couple times I’ve cut it too close leaving the house for one of my cousin’s appointments. It’s not constant, but enough that my wife and I have noticed it, if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have my normal ups and downs like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or stopped enjoying things. I still like doing the things I usually do. Is that what you mean?
When did you first notice these difficulties with focus and attention? Were they something you've had for a long time, or more recent?

I think it’s more recent, honestly. I mean, I’ve probably always had little moments here and there, like anybody, but it’s been noticeably harder for about… 11 months maybe? Since my cousin moved in with us after his surgery. That’s when I started to feel like I was having to work a bit more to keep track and stay focused. Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble focusing or staying on task when you were a child, or did this pattern start more clearly when you got older?

I guess, if I’m being honest, there were some signs when I was a kid. Nothing terrible, I don’t think, but back in grade school — before I was 12 — teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be daydreaming a lot, or I’d leave homework in my desk and not turn it in. I remember needing reminders to finish classwork, too.

I don’t know if that counts as the same kind of thing, but it was there to some extent.
As you were growing up, did you ever have trouble staying still, feel restless, or act without thinking things through — like blurting out answers in class or interrupting others?

Not that I really remember, no. I don’t think I was the kind of kid who was always getting up or causing trouble. Maybe I’d talk out of turn once in a while, like kids do, but I wouldn’t say restlessness or acting impulsively was a big issue for me. Does that answer it okay?
Have you noticed any trouble with planning out tasks, keeping things in order, or following through on steps in a project — like when you're organizing an event or preparing a big order at work?

A little bit, yes. I don’t think it’s major, but I do notice it with simple things. Like I’ll start setting up my cousin’s pill organizer, or cleaning the prep table after cooking, and then later I’ll realize I left one or two steps unfinished. It’s not like I’m ignoring it on purpose — I just sort of think I’m done, and then I see I missed something. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, have you noticed that these issues with focus and forgetfulness have been present across most areas of your life, or do they seem to come and go depending on the situation?

I think it’s more than just one situation, yeah… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

At home it’s caused some tension, especially with my cousin’s care. My wife sometimes feels like she can’t fully count on me to remember everything, and I feel bad about that. And with catering-type tasks, even small ones, I’ve had to double-check or redo things so they don’t get mixed up.

So I guess it does show up in different areas, not constantly, but enough that it’s noticeable. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel like these attention and memory issues are a change from how you used to function, or have they always been about the same throughout your life?

I think it’s mostly been there a long time, honestly. I don’t know if I always recognized it that way, but even back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but kind of… daydreaming a lot. I’d leave homework in my desk or need reminders to finish classwork.

It wasn’t like I was trying to be difficult or anything, and I did okay in some ways, so I don’t want to overstate it. But looking back, it probably wasn’t a brand-new change. Does that make sense?
Have these difficulties with attention and forgetfulness ever caused significant problems in your work, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

I wouldn’t say it’s been severe, but… yes, it has caused some problems.

Mostly at home, with my cousin’s care. My wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t always count on me to remember every step, and I understand why she feels that way, even if it’s hard to admit.

And with the catering-type things, I’ve had to go back and double-check or redo little tasks so the small jobs don’t get mixed up. It’s manageable, I think, but it has caused tension and extra work. Is that the sort of “significant” you mean?
Would you say your attention and memory issues have stayed about the same throughout your life, or do you feel like they’ve gotten noticeably worse in the past year or so compared to before?

I think it’s been there in some form for a long time, but it has felt noticeably harder more recently… maybe for about 11 months or so.

That’s around when my cousin moved in with us after surgery, and I guess having that added responsibility made it stand out more. I don’t know if that means it truly got worse, or just that I had more to keep track of, but compared to before, yes, it’s been more noticeable this past year.
Have you ever had trouble with things like managing your time well, sticking to a schedule, or deciding what to do first when you have multiple tasks?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s a major issue, but… maybe sometimes? I do try to keep a schedule, and I usually manage if I write things down or have things laid out clearly.

When there are several things at once, I can get a little unsure what to start with first, but I don’t know if that’s beyond what most people deal with. Time can get away from me a bit, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever experienced any symptoms like hearing voices, seeing things that others don't, or having strange or unusual thoughts that you're not sure are real?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people didn’t seem to see.

As far as unusual thoughts… I mean, I worry about forgetting things or not doing things right, but I don’t think I’ve had thoughts where I wasn’t sure what was real. I hope that answers what you mean.
Have you noticed any trouble starting tasks even when you know you need to, or finding it hard to make decisions about what to do next, even for everyday things?

I don’t know that I’d call it a big problem, exactly. I mean, I can usually get going if something really has to be done.

There are times I sort of sit with it longer than I should, or I’ll think, “What should I do first?” even with normal household things. But I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by trouble starting tasks, or if that’s just me being a little slow to organize myself. Does that make sense?

Looking back over the past few years, have you noticed any significant decline in your overall thinking or memory abilities — like remembering recent events, learning new information, or handling complex tasks — that feels worse than just normal forgetfulness or distraction?

I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like a big decline, no. I mean, I can be forgetful or lose track of things here and there, but it doesn’t feel like my memory or thinking has gotten steadily worse over the past few years.

Learning new things might take me a little longer than it used to, but I’m not sure that’s more than normal aging or just not paying close enough attention. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
